description: This chapter establishes the relationship between the time taken to complete a given task and work efficiency. It is a crucial arithmetic topic for competitive exams.

sections.title: Basic Concepts
sections.description: Work and Time are inversely related to each other. The rate at which work is completed is called Efficiency.

key_concepts.explanation: The total task that needs to be done. It is often considered as 1 unit or 100%.
The amount of work done in a specific unit of time (like a day or an hour). It is inversely proportional to time.

results: If the ratio of efficiencies of A and B is x:y, then the ratio of time taken by them will be y:x.

sections.title: Unitary Method
sections.description: In this method, the entire work is assumed to be 1, and the fraction of work done in a single day or hour is calculated.

equations: A's 1 day's work = 1 / Total days taken by A to complete the work

steps.title: Find 1 Day's Work
steps.detail: Find the 1 day's work of the given individuals by taking the reciprocal of their total time.

steps.title: Find Combined Work
steps.detail: If A and B work together, add their 1 day's work: (1/A + 1/B).

steps.title: Find Total Time
steps.detail: Take the reciprocal of the combined 1 day's work to get the total time required.

cases.condition: When A and B work together
results: Total time taken = (x × y) / (x + y), where x and y are the individual days taken by A and B respectively.

sections.title: LCM Method
sections.description: This is an advanced and faster alternative to the Unitary Method. The total work is assumed to be the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the given times to avoid fractions.

key_concepts.explanation: Find the LCM of the times taken by all individuals and assume it as the total units of work.

steps.title: Find LCM
steps.detail: Calculate the LCM of all given days or hours. This will be your Total Work.

steps.title: Calculate Per Day Efficiency
steps.detail: Divide the Total Work by the time of each individual to find their personal efficiency (units per day).

steps.title: Calculate Total Time
steps.detail: Divide the Total Work by the combined total efficiency of the required individuals.

cases.condition: When a person leaves before completion
results: Calculate the work done by that person and subtract it from the total work. Divide the remaining work by the efficiency of the remaining people.

sections.title: Chain Rule and MDH Formula
sections.description: When a group of people works on a task together, this formula establishes the relationship between time, work, and the number of workers.

key_concepts.explanation: The total number of persons or machines assigned to the task.
D is the number of working days, and H is the number of working hours per day.

cases.condition: If Work and Hours are constant
results: M1 × D1 = M2 × D2 (Fewer people = More days, More people = Fewer days)

sections.title: Work and Wages
sections.description: The distribution of wages is always based on the amount of work done or the efficiency of the workers, not on the time taken by them.

equations: Ratio of Wages = Ratio of Efficiencies = Ratio of Work Done

key_concepts.explanation: The total amount of money paid to the group for completing the task.

cases.condition: If all workers work for the same number of days
results: Wages will be distributed directly in the ratio of their one-day efficiency.

cases.condition: If workers work for a different number of days
results: Total wage of each person = (Their efficiency per day) × (Number of days they worked).
